ai.description: *Gegeneophis tejaswini* is a slender, 16–22 cm caecilian with a uniform dark violet-brown body. It features a distinct pale, yellowish-white collar and a terminal shield on its rounded tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis tejaswini* is uniquely distinguished from other Indian caecilians by the presence of a distinct, pale yellow stripe extending along its entire lateral body.
ai.habitat: *Gegeneophis tejaswini* inhabits moist, shaded soil within tropical evergreen forests and cardamom plantations in the Western Ghats at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Gegeneophis tejaswini* is a fossorial caecilian that remains primarily subterranean, emerging to the surface mainly during heavy monsoon rains to forage for earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis tejaswini* is oviparous and exhibits direct development. Females lay clutches of 10–15 eggs in underground burrows during the pre-monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gegeneophis tejaswini* is endemic to the Western Ghats of Karnataka, India, where it is found at elevations between 600 and 900 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Gegeneophis tejaswini* consists of a series of short, high-pitched pulses emitted from within underground burrows in moist tropical soil.
